anchor.statement: Lemma 6.2. For U, i 0 , H as in (6.17), each change H ↦→ Y i has uniformly bounded derivative factors, and R H γ consists of 14 ∆ ℓ ≤ 14 ∆ max disjoint lifts of R γ . Haar averages on the absolute, common, and band tori agree whenever the function is a pullback from the respective torus. Radial integration at fixed (z, t), torus translation, averaging, and directional Fourier inversion on zero-mean functions preserve common-torus descent and introduce no new dyadic band.

correspondence.by: Christian Garry (drafted with Claude Code; second review by ChatGPT, checked)
correspondence.note: Stated: the preimage of a native rectangle is the union of sheet rectangles, pairwise disjoint and 14^Δ in number when the chart is injective; the forward and inverse covering maps have operator norm bounded by a constant depending only on the gap bound; covering powers preserve the Haar integral of continuous functions; a coarsest band exists within the gap budget; and the temporal inverse commutes with the cover pullback up to the factor (Tg^n)^(−1). Not stated: that radial integration at fixed (z, t), torus translation and averaging preserve common-torus descent and introduce no new dyadic band; totalIntegral_periodic and cutoffAlias_periodic state only preservation of unit-lattice periodicity under a translated transport integral, which is weaker than descent from the common torus.
